title: Georgia announces a unilateral ceasefire in South Ossetia on 7 August 2008
body:
According to the Civil.ge chronology of the war, 7 August 2008 began with exchanges of fire in the South Ossetian conflict zone. Georgian intelligence intercepted calls between South Ossetian servicemen in the early morning discussing Russian troops and armour entering through the Roki Tunnel. South Ossetian leader Eduard Kokoity travelled to the Java district, near the tunnel, to meet Russian Defence Ministry representatives.

Around noon Georgia's Interior Ministry reported renewed shelling of the Georgian villages of Nuli and Avnevi. At 14:00 shelling of a Georgian peacekeeping checkpoint in Avnevi killed two peacekeepers and wounded five. At 14:30 the Georgian Defence Ministry ordered forces toward the region after intelligence indicated that Russian units near the border were preparing to move.

At 18:40 Georgian State Minister for Reintegration Temur Yakobashvili announced a unilateral ceasefire; he said he could not reach South Ossetia's chief negotiator. At 19:10 President Mikheil Saakashvili confirmed the ceasefire in a televised address, called for talks and offered concessions. Russian negotiator Yuri Popov said talks had been agreed for 13:00 on 8 August. At about 20:30 Georgia reported ceasefire violations, with fire on Avnevi and then Prisi and Tamarasheni. At 23:35 Saakashvili ordered the Joint Staff to block Russian regular units at the Roki Tunnel, neutralise firing positions targeting civilians and peacekeepers, and protect civilians in the region. A cyberattack on Georgia also began that night.
